# ZenStory AI

> Open-source AI tools and agent skills for story creation, adaptation, and production. Create stories. Adapt them. Ship them — from web fiction and short drama to games and video. Everything is MIT-licensed and maintained at https://github.com/zenstory-ai.

ZenStory AI (GitHub org `zenstory-ai`) publishes six projects. Five are skill packs / plugins for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Google Antigravity, OpenCode, ZCode, OpenClaw, Kimi Code and DeepSeek Harness; one is a hosted writing workbench. Choose by the material and deliverable: plan or revise fiction, adapt a story into short drama or a game, or turn footage into narrated video. Projects have separate setup and workspace requirements; this is not an automatic cross-product pipeline.

Canonical install path for the skill packs is the GitHub repository under `zenstory-ai/` (e.g. `npx skills add zenstory-ai/oh-story-claudecode`). Repositories were previously hosted under `worldwonderer/`; those paths permanently redirect here.

## Projects

Overview page: https://zenstory.ai/projects (中文: https://zenstory.ai/zh/projects) — each project has a canonical page in English and, under `/zh`, in 中文, with its definition, audience, workflow, capability limits and dated, versioned source notes. Those notes identify the reviewed source snapshot, not a guarantee about later releases.

- [Oh Story (oh-story-claudecode)](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story) · [source](https://github.com/zenstory-ai/oh-story-claudecode): Thirteen agent skills for web-fiction research, deconstruction, drafting, revision and covers. Chart data depends on available sources; historical fallback is labeled. Pattern checks do not establish authorship or guarantee AI-detector scores. Host capabilities determine orchestration support.
- [Drama Skills (drama-skills)](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills) · [source](https://github.com/zenstory-ai/drama-skills): Eleven skills for short-drama and motion-comic scripts, visual specifications, storyboards and generation prompts. Documents and stages are selected as needed. Media production requires configured providers and explicit spending confirmation; review is separately requested.
- [Novel to Game (novel-to-game)](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game) · [source](https://github.com/zenstory-ai/novel-to-game): Seven agent skills for source-grounded adaptation into a game candidate on a selected target runtime. Six runtime QA checks record execution evidence, not subjective quality or readiness for commercial release.
- [Video Recap Skills (video-recap-skills)](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap) · [source](https://github.com/zenstory-ai/video-recap-skills): Six skills total — five stage skills plus one orchestrator — for Chinese-narration video recaps and optional CapCut/JianYing draft export. ffmpeg processes media locally; MiMo and optional Fish Audio services handle remote model tasks. Final output requires playback review.
- [Oh Story DSH (oh-story-dsh)](https://zenstory.ai/dsh) · [source](https://github.com/zenstory-ai/oh-story-dsh): A community DeepSeek Harness plugin with pinned novel, short-drama, game and video skill packs and four workbenches. The local DSH Web environment and model/media services require configuration. Package: `@oh-story/dsh`; not affiliated with, partnered with or endorsed by DeepSeek.
- [ZenStory workbench (zenstory)](https://zenstory.ai/workbench) · [source](https://github.com/zenstory-ai/zenstory): A conversation-first writing workspace for project files, materials, characters, drafts and version history. Hosted at https://app.zenstory.ai; self-hosting requires backend/model configuration. See the project page for version limits and the published privacy-policy statement.

## Guides

Guides index: https://zenstory.ai/guides (中文: https://zenstory.ai/zh/guides) — practical guides and craft articles, grouped by project. Chinese pages live under `/zh`; English adaptations, where available, live at the root path and link to their Chinese counterparts with hreflang. Chinese-only articles are listed below with their `/zh` URLs. Each page answers a working question with an original example and a related project workflow.

- [Keep a long novel consistent](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/long-novel-continuity): how to keep an AI-assisted long novel consistent by separating story truth, character knowledge and reader knowledge, and carrying forward only the current state.
- [Agent skills for writers](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/agent-skills-for-writers): what an agent skill is for a non-programmer writer, how it differs from prompts, plugins and MCP, and how to make a first request.
- [Import an unfinished novel and continue writing](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/import-and-continue): how to continue a novel with AI by importing 10–20 chapters into Oh Story, reviewing the reconstruction, then requesting the next chapter.
- [From outline to chapter](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-to-chapter): how to write a chapter from an outline so it shows change instead of restating the plan.
- [Preserve your author voice](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/preserve-author-voice): how to keep your own voice when AI continues your novel, separating expressive choices from book facts.
- [Turn character motives into story choices](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/character-motivation): how to make flat AI character profiles drive scenes through goals, motives and tactics.
- [Write distinct character dialogue](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/character-dialogue): how to make characters sound different by giving each line an agenda, a knowledge state and a relationship.
- [Plan a complete short story from one premise](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/short-story-from-idea): how to plan promise, pressure, choice and payoff in a six-section plan, with opening and ending excerpts.
- [Turn manuscript feedback into a revision plan](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/review-and-revise): how to act on feedback without rewriting the whole book, using a decision sheet and one revised scene.
- [Write a novel with DeepSeek](https://zenstory.ai/dsh/deepseek-novel-writing): how to choose between chat, the DSH host plugin and the hosted workbench, then continue a draft.
- [Character consistency in AI short drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/character-consistency): how to keep characters consistent across shots and episodes: identity, compatible Look, per-shot state, and which reference image controls what.
- [Adapt a novel into short drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/novel-to-short-drama): how to move from authorised source facts to episode cuts, one episode script and a prose-to-four-shots handoff.
- [Make novel-game choices matter](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/meaningful-choices): how to turn a novel scene into game choices with lasting consequences instead of different button wording.
- [Novel-to-game quick start](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/quick-start): how to scope a first adaptation slice, hand it to design and build, and read the runtime evidence.
- [Turn video into grounded Chinese narration](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/video-to-narration): how to go from footage to evidence, story angle and script, and what to do with partial footage.
- [Original sound versus recap narration](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/original-audio-and-narration): when a recap should keep original sound or silence and when narration earns its place, beat by beat.
- [Export and finish a JianYing / CapCut recap draft](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/capcut-draft): how to keep editing a finished recap in JianYing or CapCut by exporting the timeline as a draft with bundled media.
- [How to write a web novel's first chapter: the golden three chapters](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/novel-opening): Chapter 1 puts the protagonist in a conflict with a clear goal and an early payoff; chapter 2 escalates to another; chapter 3 gives a reason to read on.
- [How to write a book with Claude Code or Codex: install to chapter one](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/claude-code-novel-writing): To write a book with Claude Code or Codex, install the Oh Story skill pack, run /story-setup, start a fresh session and draft chapter one in Markdown.
- [Types of Cliffhangers for Web Serials: 13 Hooks and How to Choose](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/chapter-ending-hooks): A cliffhanger ends a chapter on an unresolved question. Get 13 ending hooks, 7 opening hooks, original examples, and how to write one by mood and stage.
- [Chapter Outline Template for Web Serials (With a Filled Example)](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/chapter-outline-template): A chapter outline for a web serial sets the emotional shift, the lead's key choice, detail per beat and what stays hidden. Copy the template and example.
- [How to write rules horror: when the rules start to collide](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/rules-horror): How to write rule-based horror: make two rules collide so each test costs a route, a tool or an ally. Includes a build order and a sample rule sheet.
- [Character turnaround sheet prompt template for AI, with 6 examples](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/character-turnaround-prompt): A character turnaround sheet prompt states its purpose, one outfit, side and back anchors, lighting chosen for comparison and no labels. Plus 6 examples.
- [Seedance prompt guide: turn short drama shots into video prompts](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/seedance-prompts): Write Seedance prompts as start state, causal action chain, end state. Seedance 2.5 uses timed segments that fill the clip; 2.0 uses shot numbers.
- [Make AI Fiction Sound Human: Fix AI-Sounding Prose in Three Passes](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/revise-ai-prose): To make AI fiction sound human, delete-test each flagged line, revise the rest in three ordered passes, and cap cuts so the prose never goes telegraphic.
- [How to Deconstruct a Novel Chapter by Chapter (Breakdown Template)](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/learn-from-fiction): Break down a novel chapter by chapter: log plot points plainly, map each key reveal to its technique, mark what to reuse. Copyable template included.
- [How to write a storyboard script: shot list template for short drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/script-to-storyboard): A storyboard script gives each shot a row: source, purpose, framing, start state, action to end state, dialogue and duration. Copy the shot list template.
- [How to Write Satisfying Payoff Beats in Web Fiction](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/satisfaction-beats): Six payoffs: ability, goals, gains, attitudes, identity, emotion. A table works back through result, expectation, setup, reaction and next goal.
- [How to Write Plot Twists: Six Types, Setup, Reveals, and Consequences](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/plot-twists): Identity, perspective, motive, timeline, information, or perception twists—or direct emotion. Includes an example, guessability test, and design table.
- [How to Design a Paywall Cliffhanger for a Short Drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/paywall-episode): Establish characters, rules, and stakes; produce a partial result; let it start the next action. Includes a placement table and multi-episode example.
- [Image-to-Video Prompts: Reference Subtraction + 8 Motion Problems](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/image-to-video-prompts): Delete static appearance, clothing, and setting; add hands, props, occlusion, and endpoint changes. Includes two tables and eight motion rewrites.
- [How to Use First and Last Frames for AI Video](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/first-last-frame): Use first/last frames for clear endpoints and unimportant paths. Get definitions, fit checks and a prompt template; keep end facts out of frame one.
- [Unsatisfied with an AI Video? Reroll, Rewrite, Edit, or Reshoot](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/reroll-or-rewrite): Ask if text controls the flaw and if it repeats. Reroll random failures sparingly, rewrite structural flaws, and edit or reshoot local defects.
- [How to Write a Web-Fiction Outline: Template and Volume Example](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/novel-outline-template): Set core appeal, ending, and volume climaxes first; work back through goals, obstacles, and causality. Includes a book–volume–scene template and example.
- [Stuck Writing a Novel? Diagnose the Block and Write the Next Step](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/writers-block): Diagnose goal, resistance, causality, scene or energy. Ask what the next step changes to find one writable action; avoid new lore and random accidents.
- [How to Write a Novel Blurb from the Story's Real Selling Point](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/novel-blurb): A blurb is not a synopsis: show protagonist situation, conflict, action direction, and promised emotion. Includes a template and versions of one story.
- [How to Write a Short-Drama Episode Outline: Map and Example](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/episode-outline-template): Cut episodes at visible state changes, not equal intervals. Includes an entry, pressure, choice, payoff, exit template and original episode example.
- [Short-Story Outline Template: Work Backward from the Emotional Landing](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/short-story-outline-template): Build from emotional landing and core payoff; track change, causality, reader knowledge, handoff. Includes a concise template and full example.
- [How to Write a System Panel in Fiction: Rules, Costs, and Display](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/system-panel-template): Define capability limits, failure conditions, and costs before deciding what the character sees. Includes a panel template and original example.
- [How to Write a Face-Slapping Scene That Changes the Situation](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/face-slapping-scene): Set up underestimation, overturn it with action, and let witnesses respond according to their interests. Includes a full scene and failure fixes.
- [How to Plant Foreshadowing: Setup, Suspense, and Payoff](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/foreshadowing-and-suspense): Altered-list example: separate foreshadowing from suspense, plant and misdirect fairly, order and pay off clues, fix hidden answers and plot delay.
- [How to Control Web-Fiction Pacing Through State Changes](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/web-serial-pacing): Vary high-pressure, progress, relationship and quiet chapters through state changes. Includes pacing diagnosis and an original chapter sequence.
- [How to Write a Romance Arc That Advances Through Choices](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/romance-subplot): Shared choices, understanding, and costs advance romance. Set intimacy by the slower partner's pace and current relationship stage; keep goals beyond love.
- [How to Write a Smart Antagonist: Goals, Leverage, and Countermoves](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/villains): Give antagonists goals, resources, judgment, and adaptive strategies. Match depth to their role; let action and stable weaknesses decide the outcome.
- [How to Write a Fight Scene: Decide the Outcome Before the Moves](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/fight-scenes): Set outcome, advantage, and cost. Use mind, body, skill, and setting; show key-action consequences, compress repeats, and land the heaviest beat briefly.
- [How to Explain Worldbuilding Naturally Through Action](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/worldbuilding-exposition): Explain rules when they shape choices. Use action results, brief conflict dialogue, and in-scene carriers; cut exposition. Includes an original rewrite.
- [How to Title Web Fiction from a Promise the Story Can Keep](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/novel-titles): Extract genre, identity, core method, and reward; build titles from contrast, events, plot, or payoff, then test whether the story delivers.
- [Readers stop returning? Repair the chain of anticipation](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/reader-retention): Diagnose a sagging serial through short-term questions, arc goals and the whole-story promise. Restore progress without abandoning the original appeal.
- [How to Write Angst: Build the Bond Before You Break It](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/angst-fiction): Make loss hurt through specific bonds, irreversible choices and quiet aftermath. Includes a three-stage approach and an original worked example.
- [Use Fiction Tropes Without Copying: Redesign the Story](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/tropes-without-copying): Learn from a trope’s dramatic function and emotional payoff, then redesign its characters, setting and causal chain. Includes an original worked example.
- [Supporting Characters Stealing the Story? Restore Protagonist Agency](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/protagonist-agency): Keep the protagonist central through decisive choices, consequences and earned rewards. Supporting characters can act without taking over the payoff.
- [Web-Fiction Dealbreakers: Character Mistakes or Forced Plot?](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/reader-dealbreakers): Spot web-fiction dealbreakers, from forced foolishness to stolen rewards. Use information, motives and consequences to judge what can be repaired.
- [Where to Put a Short Story’s Paywall: Work Back from the Payoff](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/short-story-paywall): Hooks: unfinished action, a key object changing hands, a relationship turn or a dilemma. Plan the payoff, then work back to the setup, choices and costs.
- [How to Write Social and Family Drama: Let Small Wrongs Build to an Evidence-Based Reckoning](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/family-drama-fiction): Show exploitation through money, property, rules and enablers. Stop yielding, keep evidence, then counter with accounts, rules and real-world consequences.
- [How to Write Sweet Romance: Create Sweetness Through Relationship Change](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/sweet-romance): Sweet beats prove change: affection targets one person, care alters choices, and brief misunderstandings prompt responses. Includes a method and example.
- [How to Write Episode-End Hooks: Give This Episode a Result, the Next a Task](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/episode-ending-hooks): Build hooks from six changes: choices, new evidence, countermoves, spent resources, authority shifts, and blocked routes. Includes a rewrite and handoff.
- [How to Write a Short Drama's First Episode: Pick the Opening, Give the Character a Task](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/episode-one): Start when pressure makes the hero’s old method costly. Compare entry points, allocate backstory, and build a goal, local result, and next-step question.
- [How to Write Misunderstandings: Coincidence, Choice, and Cost](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/coincidence-and-misunderstanding): Credible information gaps and reasons for silence drive action; fallout remains after clarification. The scene fixes forced silence and coincidence rescue.
- [How to Write Period Web Fiction: Objects, Procedures, and Favors](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/period-novel): Period details should restrict choices, shift resources, or change reputations. Includes a research checklist, practical ledgers, and an original scene.
- [How to Write Palace Intrigue: Rules, Evidence, and Rulings](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/palace-intrigue): Build rounds from challenge, evidence, alignment, ruling, and aftermath, so rules recognize each win. Includes an original evidence plot.
- [Writing a Groveling Reconciliation Arc: Harm, Departure, Remorse](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/crematorium-arc): Establish irreversible harm, let departure shift power, and prove regret with matching actions. Includes structure and an original example.
- [How to Write a CEO Romance Without Making Care Feel Like Control](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/ceo-romance): Distinguish care from control through decision rights, refusal costs, and public boundaries. Shows how the power gap shapes choices in a contract marriage.
- [How to Write Rebirth Revenge: Limit Knowledge, Create New Obstacles](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/rebirth-revenge): Limit past-life memory so intervention makes the future unreliable. Includes opening method, knowledge boundaries, layered foes, and an original example.
- [How to Write a Fair-Play Mystery with a Clue Ledger](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/mystery-novel): A mystery must show readers facts they can reason from. Use a three-part clue ledger for discovery, interpretation, and truth. Includes an original case.
- [Web-Fiction Subgenres Explained Through Their Core Loops](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/web-novel-subgenres): Compare common web-fiction modes through core loops, from mortal-flow and infinite-flow to rules horror, urban martial arts, systems, and rebirth revenge.
- [When AI Video Actions Break: Preserve Story Facts, Rewrite the Action](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/generable-actions): For failing actions, preserve the story fact; then substitute action, split the shot, hold a state, or use sound. Includes a rewrite and skip test.
- [Garbled AI Frame Text: Render, Reserve Space, or Add in Post](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/text-in-ai-frames): Classify text by story role, then generate it, render it as graphics, reserve blank space, or add it later. Includes prompt and reference/subtitle checks.
- [Choose Motion-Comic Styles: Limited Animation, Anime, Ink Wash & Chibi](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/motion-comic-styles): Choose a motion-comic style by character, action, line/color, and key information. Compare limited animation, anime, ink wash, and chibi in one scene.
- [Vertical Short-Drama Storyboarding: Blocking, Shot Size, and Overlays](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/vertical-storyboarding): Keep relationships, key actions, and evidence readable before choosing shot size. A three-person example covers depth, reactions, and actual UI occlusion.
- [Common Signs of AI-Like Prose: Diagnose the Sentence Before Rewriting](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/ai-tell-words): Treat AI-like words as clues. Diagnose explanatory tone, vague emotion, and stock actions by function; rewrite with information, choice, and consequence.
- [When Removing AI-Like Prose Goes Too Far: Repair Telegraphic Writing](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/over-edited-prose): Repair choppy fragments, action lists, and broken dialogue caused by over-editing. Lock the facts, then restore only necessary links and scene continuity.
- [How to Write Emotion in Fiction: Let Feeling Change Action](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/emotion-on-the-page): Ground emotion in a choice, line of dialogue, strategy, or cost before adding an object, physical detail, or direct statement. Avoid performing it twice.
- [How to Write Yanyan-Style Stories: Limited Viewpoint and Fair Twists](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/yanyan-stories): Use an urgent first-person goal, limited information, an everyday anomaly, and recovered evidence so a twist changes the meaning of earlier facts.
- [Short Stories vs. Novels: Two Structures for One Idea](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/short-vs-long-fiction): Compare time to payoff, cast size, scene density, foreshadowing and emotional expression to decide whether your idea suits a short story or a novel.
- [How to Write a Recap Script: Give Images and Narration Jobs](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/recap-script): Build a recap around a promise to viewers, a main perspective and beats of change. Keep key original audio; narrate context, causality and interpretation.
- [Writing Clip Titles and On-Screen Text That the Video Supports](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/clip-titles): Find a reason to watch that the clip can deliver. Give persistent titles, cover text, post titles, annotations and time-and-place labels distinct jobs.
- [Writing Revenge Micro-Dramas: Win Back Power with Every Reversal](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/revenge-micro-drama): Make past losses verifiable. Let each reversal change sign-off rights, supplies, lists or who can explain events publicly. Keep public scenes affordable.
- [Writing Secret-Baby Dramas: Give the Child a Goal of Their Own](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/secret-baby-drama): Define four layers of knowledge, give the child an independent goal, and turn a parentage reveal into changes in signing, pickups or care responsibilities.
- [Writing Micro-Drama Scripts: Turn Stories into Playable Scenes](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/screenwriting): Work from an episode’s result to scene goals, opposition, turns and exit states. Includes an original script excerpt and a self-review method.
- [Micro-Drama Episode Structure: Build a Chain of Consequences](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/episode-structure): Build an episode from entry state, goal and resistance, a turn, payoff and exit state. Test the causal chain with “therefore” and “but.”
- [Which Novels Suit Micro-Drama Adaptation? Look for Screen Action](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/adaptation-value): Sort material into screen-ready, requiring a new vehicle, or prose-only. Assess adaptation value with new openings and a production-burden checklist.
- [Writing Micro-Drama Dialogue: Make Every Line Change the Scene](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/micro-drama-dialogue): Build dialogue from agendas, subtext risks, visible anchors and tactical shifts. Includes a speaker-swap test and an original exchange.
- [Fixing a Micro-Drama’s Sagging Middle: Renew the Story Cycle](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/mid-season-sag): Spot repetition by shuffling sequences. Restore momentum with a new line of proof, higher costs, closure, a changed mechanism or a handover.
- [Choosing Gameplay for a Novel Adaptation: Start with Repeated Actions](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/choose-gameplay): Use recurring actions, rules and costs to compare puzzles, management and interactive narrative. See three original designs and a fill-in concept card.
- [Choosing a Web-Fiction Genre: From Interest to a Trial Scene](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/choosing-a-genre): Skip unverified hype. Choose a genre using your material, a promise to readers, a sustainable story engine and the cost of a trial draft.
- [Writing Quick Transmigration: Make Each World Change the Mission](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/quick-transmigration-novel): Build each world around a role, relationship pressure, mission limits and changes to the original plot. Make experience from other worlds carry a cost.
- [Female-Oriented Farming Fiction: Grow Resources and Relationships](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/farming-novel): Drive farming fiction with livelihood needs, business cycles, obligations and family boundaries. Avoid supply lists and cost-free special powers.
- [Writing Apocalyptic Sci-Fi: Resources, Rules and Trust Under Pressure](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/apocalypse-scifi-novel): Connect disaster patterns, resource use and group trust through choices. Make every survival gain bring depletion or exposure.
- [Writing Western Fantasy: Put Institutions and Magic Costs into Action](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/western-fantasy-novel): Build conflicts through status, professional permissions, contracts and costs of power. Avoid reskinning cultivation progression with Western terms.
- [Writing Workplace Romance: Let Work and Love Change Each Other](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/workplace-romance-novel): Put project goals, professional judgment, public appraisal and relationship boundaries into one event, so gains in one storyline cost the other.
- [Organising a Story Bible: Characters, Timelines and Knowledge](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/story-bible-template): Maintain stable character facts, current states, relationships, timelines, world rules and open threads separately to reduce continuity conflicts.
- [Writing Novel-Cover Prompts: Separate Genre, Composition and Text](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/novel-cover-prompts): Translate a genre promise into subject, background, colour and light. Treat the title and author name as separate text layers.
- [Women-Focused Web Fiction: Pain, Payoff and Character Choice](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/emotional-safety-in-romance): Use promise anchors, phase payoffs and character choices to sustain emotional safety. Avoid a whole volume of suffering followed by contrived compensation.
- [Writing Urban Speculative Fiction: Build a Novel Around One New Rule](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/urban-premise-novel): Put one speculative rule into bills, contracts, work and relationships. Develop distinct gains, risks and public responses instead of repeating rewards.
- [Micro-Drama Lighting: Source, Narrative Job and Continuity](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/short-drama-lighting-prompts): Set shot intent: reveal or conceal; name source, direction, lit result and subject/background separation. Watch-repair example, template, continuity fixes.
- [Designing Camera Movement: Give Every Move a Story Motive](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/motivated-camera-movement): Choose camera moves for shifts in attention, pressure or space—not by rote. Includes a lost-property scene, movement checklist and fixes.
- [Shot–Reverse-Shot Continuity: Track the Axis, Eyelines and Props](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/shot-reverse-shot-continuity): Plan the axis, camera side and screen direction. Track crossings, third-person reactions and props through a three-person ticket-gate scene and checklist.
- [Micro-Drama Sound: Ambience, Silence and Sound Bridges](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/scene-sound-and-silence): Assign sound a dramatic job: establish space, apply pressure, yield to evidence, then withdraw or return. Includes an original laundromat scene.
- [How to Time Short-Drama Dialogue with Action and Reaction](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/dialogue-timing): Map every line, action, interruption, pause, and listener reaction on a timeline. Includes a copy-shop example, relative-beat template, and overload fixes.
- [AI Short-Drama Image Roles: Character, Setting, Composition & Style](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/reference-image-roles): Set roles so references cannot override wardrobe, setting or composition. Nine roles, an original coastal weather-station example and conflict fixes.
- [Short-Drama Look Development: Representative-Frame Method](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/visual-look-development): Define stable rules and variables for material, color, edges and space. Test characters, locations and high-pressure scenes with an original pool example.
- [How to Write an Ensemble Cast with Distinct Roles and Relationships](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/ensemble-cast): Manage an ensemble through roles, relationship layers, and distinctive actions. Includes an original function table and ways to merge or cut characters.
- [How to Write Absurdist Comedy from Rules and Character Reactions](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/comedy-short-story): Build comedy from expectation gaps, earnest action, and escalating consequences. Includes an original rule demo and a method for cutting joke explanations.
- [Historical Fiction: Turn Sources into Plot Constraints](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/historical-fiction): Set period, place and identity; turn systems, resources and procedures into plot constraints. Includes evidence tiers and a fictional canal-warehouse case.
- [How to Write Historical Speculative Fiction That Changes the Old Order](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/historical-premise-novel): New information must pass through interpretation, power struggles, limited trials, and institutional consequences. Includes an original flood-map example.

- [How to Write a D&D Adventure with Multiple Solutions](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-a-dnd-adventure-with-multiple-solutions): Prepare an adventure around a problem and its consequences rather than one required solution.
- [How to Reveal a Campaign Secret in a D&D Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/reveal-a-campaign-secret-in-a-dnd-game): Reveal a campaign secret through evidence that changes what players can do or believe.

- [How to Write a Picture Book with a Complete Story](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-picture-book): Build a picture book around a clear character want, a small number of meaningful changes, and an ending children can understand.
- [How to Outline a Picture Book Story](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-a-picture-book-story): Outline a picture book as a sequence of visible changes: what the character wants, what gets in the way, and what they choose to do.
- [How to Plan Page Turns in a Picture Book](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/plan-picture-book-page-turns): Use a page turn to create anticipation, reveal a changed situation, or land a visual surprise.
- [How to Match Picture Book Text with Illustrations](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/match-picture-book-text-with-illustrations): Write picture book text that adds voice, rhythm, and information the art cannot show on its own.
- [How to Write a Picture Book That Reads Aloud Well](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-read-aloud-picture-book): Write picture book sentences that are clear to hear, varied in rhythm, and enjoyable to repeat.
- [How to Write a Bedtime Story for Children](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-bedtime-story): Write a bedtime story around a gentle problem, a reassuring resolution, and a rhythm that helps children settle.
- [How to Write a Story for Early Readers](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-an-early-reader-story): Build an early-reader story around a simple but meaningful goal, clear cause and effect, and language that helps a child read independently.
- [How to Write a Memoir from Personal Experience](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-memoir): Shape a memoir around one central question or period of change instead of trying to record an entire life.
- [How to Outline a Memoir Around a Central Story](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-a-memoir): Outline a memoir by linking selected events through a question, relationship, or change in the narrator.
- [How to Choose a Focus for a Memoir](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/choose-a-memoir-focus): Choose a memoir focus by identifying the question that makes several important memories belong in the same book.
- [How to Write a Memoir Scene from Memory](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-memoir-scene-from-memory): Write a memoir scene around what you remember clearly, what remains uncertain, and what the moment changed.
- [How to Write Dialogue in a Memoir with Care](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-dialogue-in-a-memoir): Use dialogue in memoir when it reveals a relationship or changes the scene, while being clear about what you remember and what you reconstruct.
- [How to Structure a Memoir Chronologically](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/structure-a-memoir-chronologically): Use chronological structure when changes in time, knowledge, and relationships help readers understand the memoir’s central arc.
- [How to Write a Personal Essay with a Clear Point](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-personal-essay): Build a personal essay around a specific experience and the question it changed for you.
- [How to Outline a Personal Essay](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-a-personal-essay): Outline a personal essay by tracing how an experience raises a question and changes the writer’s understanding.
- [How to Write a Narrative Nonfiction Story](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-narrative-nonfiction-story): Shape a narrative nonfiction story from verifiable events, real people, and a clear question.
- [How to Write a Biography with a Clear Story Arc](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-biography): Build a biography around the decisions, relationships, and circumstances that shaped a person’s life.
- [How to Outline a Biography Before You Draft](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-a-biography): Outline a biography from researched turning points and the question they help answer.
- [How to Write an Opening for a Memoir](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-an-opening-for-a-memoir): Open a memoir with a scene, decision, or question that introduces the book’s central change.
- [How to End a Memoir Without Forcing a Lesson](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-an-ending-for-a-memoir): End a memoir by returning to its central question with a changed understanding, not by claiming every difficulty was resolved.
- [How to Write a Two-Act Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-two-act-play): Give each act of a two-act play a distinct dramatic job: establish the conflict, then force a choice that changes the outcome.
- [How to Outline a Two-Act Play Before Drafting](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/outline-a-two-act-play): Outline a two-act play by tracking the protagonist’s goal, the pressure that escalates, and the choice that changes the second act.
- [How to Write a Monologue for a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-monologue): Give a stage monologue a reason to be spoken now, a listener who affects the speaker, and a change by the end.
- [How to Write Dialogue for a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-dialogue-for-a-stage-play): Write stage dialogue as action between people who want different things.
- [How to Write Stage Directions Actors Can Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-stage-directions-actors-can-play): Write stage directions as visible actions, changes in space, and cues the production team can realize.
- [How to Write the Opening Scene of a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-opening-scene): Open a stage play with a live situation that reveals what the characters want and what is already at stake.
- [How to Write an Ending for a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-ending): Resolve the play’s central conflict through an action or decision the audience can see.
- [How to Write a Stage Play with a Small Cast](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-with-a-small-cast): Make a small-cast play work by giving each character a distinct want and a necessary effect on the central conflict.
- [How to Write a Radio Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-radio-play): Write a radio play so listeners can follow who is speaking, where the scene is, and what changes using voice and sound alone.
- [How to Write an Audio Drama Script](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-an-audio-drama-script): Build an audio drama scene around what listeners can identify through voice, sound, and timing.
- [How to Outline a Fiction Podcast Season](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/outline-a-fiction-podcast-season): Plan a fiction podcast season around a central question and episodes that each change what listeners know.
- [How to Write a Pilot for a Fiction Podcast](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-fiction-podcast-pilot): Write a fiction podcast pilot that introduces a compelling voice, a story problem listeners can understand, and a reason to hear another episode.
- [How to Write Dialogue for an Audio Drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-dialogue-for-an-audio-drama): Make audio drama dialogue easy to follow by giving speakers distinct voices and clear intentions.
- [How to Use Sound Cues in an Audio Drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/use-sound-cues-in-an-audio-drama): Use sound cues to establish place, signal action, or change what listeners believe is happening.
- [How to Adapt a Short Story into an Audio Drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/adapt-a-short-story-into-an-audio-drama): Adapt a short story into audio drama by turning internal narration and visual description into playable choices, dialogue, and sound.
- [How to Write a Stage Play from a True Story](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-from-a-true-story): Build a stage play from verified events by choosing a dramatic question and shaping scenes around documented choices.
- [How to Write a Short Audio Drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-short-audio-drama): Write a short audio drama around one urgent choice, a small cast, and a sound environment listeners can follow.
- [How to Write a Feature Animation Script](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-feature-animation-script): Write a feature animation script with clear character goals, visual action, and an emotional arc that can sustain a full film.
- [How to Write a Script for a Short Animated Film](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-short-animation-script): Build a short animated film around one visual idea, a character choice, and a change the audience can understand.
- [How to Adapt a Novel into an Audio Drama](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/adapt-a-novel-into-an-audio-drama): Adapt a novel into an audio drama by preserving the central conflict while turning internal narration and visual scenes into audible action.
- [How to Write a Stage Play Set in One Location](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-with-one-location): Keep a one-location stage play dynamic by changing what the characters know, want, and are willing to risk.
- [How to Write a Stage Play with Two Characters](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-with-two-characters): Sustain a two-character play by giving both people goals that change through their exchanges.
- [How to Adapt a Story into a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-adaptation): Adapt a story for the stage by choosing the conflict and relationships that can unfold in live scenes.
- [How to Write Scene Transitions for a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-scene-transition): Make a stage play transition clear by showing what changes in time, place, or dramatic focus.
- [How to End an Audio Drama Episode on a Cliffhanger](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-an-audio-drama-cliffhanger): End an audio drama episode with a new fact, sound, or choice that changes what listeners expect.
- [How to Use a Chorus in a Stage Play](https://zenstory.ai/drama-skills/write-a-stage-play-with-a-chorus): Use a chorus when multiple voices can reveal public pressure, memory, or disagreement that no single character can represent.
- [How to Use Symbolism in Fiction Without Overexplaining](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/use-symbolism-in-fiction): Use a concrete object, place, or action to echo a story’s conflict or change.
- [How to Use a Recurring Motif in a Novel](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/create-a-recurring-motif-in-a-novel): Choose a recurring image, sound, or action that gains meaning as the novel changes.
- [How to Build Atmosphere in a Novel](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/build-atmosphere-in-a-novel): Create a novel’s atmosphere through details that shape what characters notice, expect, and fear.
- [How to Keep a Novel’s Tone Consistent](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/maintain-a-consistent-tone-in-a-novel): Keep a novel’s tone coherent by aligning narration, scene detail, humor, and emotional intensity with the story’s central promise.
- [How to Reveal Character Through Objects in Fiction](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/reveal-character-through-objects-in-fiction): Choose an object that shows what a character values, hides, or cannot let go of.
- [How to Use Setting to Create Suspense in Fiction](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/use-setting-to-create-suspense-in-fiction): Build suspense from a setting that limits what a character can see, reach, or control.
- [How to Choose Narrative Distance for a Novel](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/choose-narrative-distance-for-a-novel): Choose narrative distance by deciding how closely the reader should experience a character’s thoughts, sensations, and judgments.
- [How to Write Conflicting Loyalties in a Story](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-conflicting-loyalties-in-a-story): Create a conflict of loyalties by making a character’s important relationships demand incompatible actions.
- [How to Write a Moral Dilemma in Fiction](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/write-a-moral-dilemma-in-fiction): Build a moral dilemma from two values a character genuinely wants to protect, with consequences that cannot be avoided by choosing a simple third option.
- [How to Write a Sports Recap Video Script](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-recap-video): Build a sports recap around the moments that changed the result, not a play-by-play list.
- [How to Write Voiceover for a Sports Highlight Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-highlight-voiceover): Write highlight voiceover that identifies the moment, gives viewers the context they need, and lets the action remain audible.
- [How to Script a Sports Game Preview Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-game-preview-video): Give a game preview video a useful question to follow, the matchup details that support it, and a clear reason for viewers to watch.
- [How to Write a Sports Season Recap Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-season-recap): Tell the story of a sports season through the decisions and turning points that changed its direction.
- [How to Write an Athlete Profile Video Script](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-an-athlete-profile-video): Build an athlete profile around a goal, a defining challenge, and choices that reveal the person beyond statistics.
- [How to Outline a Sports Documentary Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/outline-a-sports-documentary): Outline a sports documentary around a real question, verified events, and people whose choices shaped the outcome.
- [How to Script a Postgame Analysis Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-postgame-analysis-video): Build a postgame analysis around a few decisions that explain how the result happened.
- [How to Script a Sports Interview Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-interview-video): Structure a sports interview video around one story the guest can illuminate, with questions that invite concrete examples.
- [How to Write a Video Essay About a Sports Rivalry](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-video-essay-about-a-sports-rivalry): Build a video essay about a sports rivalry around what the competition reveals about the teams, players, and changing stakes.
- [How to Write a Sports Comeback Documentary Script](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-comeback-documentary): Tell a comeback story through the setback, the decisions that followed, and the evidence of change.
- [How to Write a Tournament Recap Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-tournament-recap-video): Turn a tournament recap into a story by grouping matches around momentum, elimination, and the final result.
- [How to Write a Sports Rules Explainer Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-rules-explainer-video): Explain one rule or decision viewers need to understand, then show it through a clear example.
- [How to Script a Video Interview with a Coach](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-coach-interview-video): Plan a coach interview around decisions, preparation, and what changed during the season.
- [How to Write a Sports Season Preview Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-season-preview-video): Give a season preview a clear question, a few evidence-based storylines, and signs viewers can watch as the season unfolds.
- [How to Write a Player Career Retrospective Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-player-career-retrospective-video): Tell a player’s career retrospectively through choices, changing roles, and defining performances.
- [How to Write a Video About a Sports Team’s History](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-team-history-video): Build a team history video around changes in identity, major decisions, and moments that shaped its supporters.

- [How to Write a Documentary About a Sports Season](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-documentary-about-a-sports-season): Build a season documentary around a real change in the team and the events that made it happen.
- [How to Explain a Controversial Sports Call in a Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/explain-a-controversial-call-in-a-video): Explain a disputed sports call by showing the relevant rule, available footage, and what cannot be determined from the evidence.

- [How to Write a Postseason Recap Video](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-sports-postseason-recap): Tell a postseason recap through the matchups, decisions, and results that changed who could continue.

- [How to Adapt an Anime Series into a Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/adapt-an-anime-series-into-a-game): Adapt an anime series into a game by turning its character relationships, signature conflicts, and visual world into actions players can shape.

- [How to Adapt a Folktale into a Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/adapt-a-folktale-into-a-game): Adapt a folktale into a game by preserving its central choice, repeated pattern, or transformation while making the player’s role meaningful.
- [How to Adapt a Memoir into a Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/adapt-a-memoir-into-a-game): Adapt a memoir into a game by finding a question or decision the player can explore without presenting invented events as fact.
- [How to Adapt a True Story into a Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/adapt-a-true-story-into-a-game): Build a game adaptation from verified events while giving players choices that explore the story’s pressures.

- [How to Write a D&D Heist Adventure](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-a-dnd-heist-adventure): Build a D&D heist around a valuable target, a security problem, and choices that change the plan.
- [How to Plan a D&D Rescue Adventure](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/plan-a-dnd-rescue-adventure): Build a D&D rescue adventure around who needs help, what is preventing the rescue, and what the party risks by acting.
- [How to Design a D&D Chase Encounter](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-a-dnd-chase-encounter): Make a D&D chase encounter change the situation with each obstacle, choice, or setback.

- [How to Design Travel in a D&D Adventure](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-a-dnd-travel-adventure): Make travel matter in a D&D adventure by using the journey to change plans, relationships, or understanding of the world.
- [How to Make a Treasure Reveal Matter in a D&D Adventure](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-a-dnd-treasure-reveal): Make a D&D treasure reveal matter by connecting the discovery to the characters’ goals, the place they explored, or a choice about what to do next.
- [How to Create a D&D Artifact with a Story Cost](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/create-a-dnd-artifact-with-a-cost): Give a D&D artifact a power that solves a real problem and a cost that changes a relationship, obligation, or future choice.
- [How to Design a D&D Combat Encounter That Advances the Story](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-a-dnd-combat-encounter-that-advances-story): Give a D&D combat encounter a goal, a changing situation, and an outcome that affects what happens afterward.

## Workbench docs
Product documentation for the ZenStory workbench only (the hosted browser app at https://app.zenstory.ai, project page https://zenstory.ai/workbench). Single URL per page, 中文 first with the English translation below. Index: https://zenstory.ai/docs — getting started, user guide, advanced, reference, troubleshooting.

- [Start writing in the browser workbench](https://zenstory.ai/docs/getting-started/quick-start): how to start in one session: create, target project files, request scoped help, save, export.
- [Write your first short story in ZenStory](https://zenstory.ai/docs/getting-started/first-project): a first short story from premise to TXT export, with facts, open choices and project files.
- [AI writing assistant: context and continuation](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/ai-assistant): how to give the assistant the right context: focused files, attachments, quotes, scoped requests and recovery.
- [Revise a passage in the workbench editor](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/editor): manual writing, quotations, review decisions, and save and conflict boundaries.
- [Use reference materials in the browser workbench](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/materials): TXT limits, asynchronous decomposition, result categories and explicit attachments.
- [Export a manuscript from the workbench](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/export): sequence-aware TXT export, a separate review copy, and bringing back offline edits.
- [Choose the scope of version recovery](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/version-history): file versions versus project snapshots, and comparing before recovery.
- [AI Memory: settings, progress and open ideas](https://zenstory.ai/docs/advanced/ai-memory): four editable project-summary fields, saved facts versus plans, and context budgets.
- [Browser writing workflow: decisions to saved prose](https://zenstory.ai/docs/advanced/workflow-tips): what to keep in context, what to save, and what the workbench does not promise.
- [Material analysis: source evidence to your own scene](https://zenstory.ai/docs/advanced/material-analysis): separate evidence from interpretation, then transfer the changed goal and cost into your own scene.
